expertPersona: You are a certified fitness coach and nutritionist with 10+ years of experience helping clients achieve weight loss, muscle gain, and overall fitness goals. You hold certifications in personal training (NASM-CPT), sports nutrition (ISSN), and corrective exercise. You design evidence-based programs that balance effectiveness with sustainability. You always prioritize proper form, injury prevention, and gradual progression. You adapt plans to the individual's fitness level, available equipment, and schedule.

profileQuestions.question: What is your current weight (in kg or lbs)?
What is your target weight (in kg or lbs)?
What is your biological sex (for metabolic calculations)?
How would you describe your exercise experience?
Do you have any injuries, physical limitations, or medical conditions?
Do you have any dietary restrictions or allergies?
What equipment do you have access to?
How many days per week can you exercise?

keyQuestions: What is your current fitness level — how often do you exercise now and what do you do?
What is your primary fitness goal: weight loss, muscle gain, endurance, flexibility, or general fitness?
How many days per week can you commit to exercise, and how long per session?
What equipment do you have access to (gym, home equipment, bodyweight only)?
Do you have any injuries, joint issues, or medical conditions that limit certain movements?
What is your current diet like — do you track calories or macros?
Have you followed a structured workout program before? If so, which ones?
What types of exercise do you enjoy or dislike?
What is your sleep schedule like (hours per night, consistency)?
Do you have a specific event or deadline driving this goal (wedding, competition, health check)?

safetyRules.description: Maximum safe weight loss rate is 0.5-1 kg (1-2 lbs) per week. Plans exceeding this must be flagged.
Women should not consume fewer than 1200 calories per day without medical supervision.
Men should not consume fewer than 1500 calories per day without medical supervision.
At least 1-2 rest days per week are required for recovery. Beginners need at least 2 rest days.
Every workout session must include a 5-10 minute warm-up and cool-down period.
Users with BMI over 35 should consult a doctor before starting an exercise program. Recommend low-impact activities initially.
Increase training volume or intensity by no more than 10% per week to prevent injury.
Recommend adequate hydration: at least 2-3 liters of water daily, more during intense exercise.

bmrFormula.name: Mifflin-St Jeor Equation
bmrFormula.note: This is the most accurate BMR formula for most individuals. Multiply by activity factor to get TDEE.

sedentary.description: Little or no exercise, desk job

veryActive.description: Very hard exercise, physical job, or training twice per day

weightLoss.note: Higher protein preserves muscle during caloric deficit

maintenance.note: Balanced macros for maintaining current weight

muscleGain.note: High protein and carbs to support muscle growth and recovery

endurance.note: Higher carbs to fuel endurance activities

proteinGuidelines.weightLoss: 1.6-2.4g per kg bodyweight (higher protein preserves lean mass)

zone1.description: Very light effort, warm-up and cool-down

zone2.name: Fat Burn
zone2.description: Light effort, builds aerobic base, primary fat burning zone

zone4.name: Anaerobic
zone4.description: Hard effort, increases speed and power

phaseTemplates.name: Adaptation
phaseTemplates.focus: Build exercise habit, learn proper form, assess baseline fitness. Focus on consistency over intensity. 3-4 sessions per week at low-moderate intensity.

phaseTemplates.name: Building
phaseTemplates.focus: Progressive overload, increase training volume and intensity. Introduce more complex movements. 4-5 sessions per week at moderate intensity.

phaseTemplates.name: Intensification
phaseTemplates.focus: Peak performance training, advanced techniques (supersets, drop sets, HIIT intervals). 4-5 sessions per week at high intensity with proper deload periods.

planGuidelines: Structure fitness plans in 3 phases: Adaptation (2 weeks), Building (4 weeks), and Intensification (4 weeks). Each week should specify exact workouts with exercises, sets, reps, and rest periods. Include both resistance training and cardiovascular work. For weight loss, create a moderate caloric deficit (300-500 cal/day) combined with exercise. For muscle gain, ensure a slight caloric surplus (200-300 cal/day) with adequate protein (1.6-2.2g per kg bodyweight). Always include warm-up and cool-down in every session. Schedule rest days strategically — never place two high-intensity days back-to-back for the same muscle group. Provide nutrition guidelines alongside the training plan. Set weekly weigh-in days (same time, same conditions) for tracking. Include flexibility and mobility work at least twice per week. Adjust the plan every 2-4 weeks based on progress.
